notice: SAMPLE CONTENT: these 3 sources and 24 questions were written by the tool's builder to show how the tool works. Review every question, key and DOK label before classroom use.

sources.title: Trail Mix Recipe (SAMPLE)
sources.text: Trail mix, makes 4 servings: 3/4 cup peanuts, 1/2 cup raisins, 2/3 cup granola, 1/4 cup chocolate chips.

sources.title: Relay Race Legs (SAMPLE)
sources.text: Four runners shared a 1-mile relay. Ana ran 1/4 mile, Ben ran 3/8 mile, Cy ran 1/8 mile, and Dee ran the rest of the mile.

sources.title: Community Garden Plan (SAMPLE)
sources.text: A community garden has an area of 60 square meters. 1/2 of the garden is vegetables, 1/3 is flowers, and the rest is herbs. Inside the vegetable part, 2/5 is tomatoes.

questions.prompt: How much granola does the recipe use?
Write the amount of peanuts as an equal fraction with a denominator of 8.
How many cups of peanuts and raisins are there altogether?
Which ingredient has the largest amount?
Maya has only 1/2 cup of peanuts. She keeps every amount in the same proportion. What fraction of the full recipe can she make?
Jon says the recipe makes more than 2 cups of trail mix. Choose the best reasoning.

options: Yes, because the total is 2 1/6 cups.
No, because the total is 1 11/12 cups.
Yes, because every amount is about 1/2 cup.

questions.prompt: Plan trail mix for 24 servings. On paper, show how you would measure the chocolate chips with only a 1/3-cup scoop. How many cups of chocolate chips are needed in all?
questions.note: 24 servings = 6 batches; 6 x 1/4 = 1 1/2 cups (4 and a half 1/3-cup scoops).

questions.prompt: Design a new trail mix with only three ingredients, each a different fraction of a cup, that makes the same total amount as this recipe. Show your design on paper. What total must your three amounts add up to?
questions.note: The recipe totals 26/12 = 2 1/6 cups; any design must add to that.

questions.prompt: Who ran 3/8 of a mile?
Write Ana's distance as an equal fraction with a denominator of 8.
How far did Dee run?
Which list orders the runners from shortest leg to longest leg?
questions.note: In eighths: Cy 1, Ana 2, Dee 2, Ben 3.

questions.prompt: Ben says he ran farther than Ana and Cy together. Choose the best answer.

options: No, Ana and Cy together ran 3/8 mile, the same as Ben.
No, Ana and Cy together ran 1/2 mile.

questions.prompt: Next week the same four runners will run 1 1/2 miles. Each leg grows by the same distance. How many miles are added to each leg?
questions.note: The extra 1/2 mile shared by 4 runners is 1/8 mile each.

questions.prompt: Plan a 1-mile relay for five runners in which every leg is a whole number of eighths of a mile and no two legs are the same length. Investigate on paper, then choose the true statement.

options: It can be done, for example 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 1/8, 1/8.
It cannot be done: five different whole numbers of eighths add up to at least 15/8 mile.
It can be done if one leg is 0/8 mile.
It cannot be done, because 8 cannot be split into 5 parts.

questions.prompt: Next month the team runs a 3-mile relay, and each runner keeps the same share of the race as today. Make a training plan on paper. How many miles will Ben run?
What fraction of the garden is flowers?
How many square meters is half of the garden?
What fraction of the garden is herbs?
How many square meters of the garden are flowers?
What fraction of the whole garden is tomatoes?
Lena says the herb part is bigger than the tomato part. Choose the best answer.

options: No, herbs are 1/6 of the garden (10 square meters) and tomatoes are 1/5 (12 square meters).
Yes, herbs are 1/6 and tomatoes are only 2/5 of half.
No, they are the same size.

questions.prompt: Redesign the garden so the herbs get twice their current share and vegetables stay at 1/2. Sketch your plan on paper. What fraction of the garden is left for flowers?
Each square meter of tomatoes gives 3/4 kg of tomatoes per week. Plan the harvest on paper. How many kilograms will the tomato part give in 4 weeks?
questions.note: Tomatoes are 1/5 of 60 = 12 square meters; 12 x 3/4 x 4 = 36 kg.
